keyMessage.found: Incidents run on improvisation with no tested plan, playbook, severity scale, or record.
keyMessage.closes: Approve an incident response plan with a ransomware playbook and hold a first tabletop exercise.

categories.whatWorksToday: Users can report suspicious email with one click.

strengths.statement: Users can report suspicious email with one click.

gapFindings.title: No tested incident response plan or ransomware playbook
gapFindings.statement: Incidents are handled by whoever is available, with no confirmed playbook, no exercise, and no criteria to start recovery.

supportingFacts.fact: Playbooks for ransomware and phishing were not confirmed.
No technical or tabletop exercise has been run.
Criteria for starting recovery are not defined.

extent.notChecked: Departmental downtime procedures were not collected

gapFindings.consequence: Decisions in the first hours are improvised during an attack on a hospital that runs around the clock, and reporting duties are missed.

likelihood.rationale: No tested plan exists and the threat is active.

ops.rationale: Improvised response stops or slows hospital operations.

fin.rationale: Improvised response adds recovery cost and revenue loss.

legal.rationale: Improvised response triggers reporting duties or regulator questions.

rep.rationale: Improvised response damages patient and public trust.

safety.rationale: Improvised response delays or disrupts patient care.

data.rationale: Improvised response exposes sensitive health records.

gapFindings.title: Incident reports are not triaged, categorized, or escalated
gapFindings.statement: Reports reach IT but no steps triage, rate, or escalate them, so serious incidents cannot be told from routine ones.

supportingFacts.fact: Users can report phishing with one click, but no triage steps follow.
The contact list and out-of-band channel are only partly defined.

extent.notChecked: Past incident emails were not collected

gapFindings.consequence: A reportable event passes as routine, and CMC misses its CII reporting duty.

likelihood.rationale: Process gap that needs a reportable event before harm.

keyMessage.found: Investigations end at service restoration, and CMC cannot scope a breach to patient records.
keyMessage.closes: Define evidence steps, retain a forensic provider, and extend log retention.

gapFindings.title: Investigation records and evidence are not preserved
gapFindings.statement: CMC has only partial forensic capability and unsynchronized clocks, so evidence is weak and the entry point stays unknown.

supportingFacts.fact: Forensic capability is only partly available.
System clocks are not synchronized to a trusted source.
No steps exist to preserve incident data and its integrity.

extent.notChecked: Past incident files were not provided

gapFindings.consequence: Attackers return through the same route after recovery, and CMC cannot support a regulator inquiry.

keyMessage.closes: Write a notification procedure after verifying current CII and PDPA timelines, and prepare message templates.

extent.notChecked: Current reporting timelines were not verified

keyMessage.found: The team can contain a host, but no playbook or authority says who orders isolation of core systems.
keyMessage.closes: Record who may isolate which systems, including a night shift rule for HIS.

categories.whatWorksToday: The IT team can isolate a host, disable an account, and block an indicator.

strengths.statement: The IT team can isolate a host, disable an account, and block an indicator across the environment.

gapFindings.title: Containment ability exists but decision authority does not
gapFindings.statement: The team can isolate hosts, but no playbook or authority says who orders isolation of core systems, even at night.

supportingFacts.fact: The team can isolate a host, disable an account, and block an indicator.
No playbook sets containment steps or who may order isolation.

extent.notChecked: Authority for other systems was not reviewed

gapFindings.consequence: Delay in disconnecting lets ransomware spread to more systems and lengthens the outage.

likelihood.rationale: Governance gap that needs an attack before harm.

improvementActions.action: Approve an incident response plan with a ransomware playbook
Hold a tabletop exercise on ransomware each year
Define triage, severity, and escalation steps and start an incident log
Keep a current contact list and an out-of-band channel for responders
Define evidence preservation steps and retain a forensic provider
Synchronize system clocks to a trusted time source
Extend log retention on HIS and PACS to support scoping of affected records
Write a notification procedure with owner, timeline, and template for CII and PDPA reporting after verifying current timelines
Name communication roles and prepare message templates for patients, staff, and media
Record who may isolate which systems, including a night shift rule for HIS, in the response plan
